defects.title: Tritium release windows closed inconsistently at late times, creating mass
defects.disposition: The release-rate lookup and the step bound rounded differently near 1.3e8 s, so a window could stay open one step too long and the in-process clamp then created 7.4e-4 kg of tritium in one ensemble draw. All three comparisons now use the same form, and a history regression test runs the failing draw.

defects.title: Verifier refused every recorded package that carried a sweep
defects.disposition: The package index records the sweep scenario digest bare but the verifier compared it with a prefixed file digest, so it refused real packages with an error. It now compares the bare form, and the test fixture uses the form the packager writes.

defects.title: OKTAVIAN-Al validation runner scored the wrong tally values
defects.disposition: The runner compared a per-cell partial tally without summing over cells and read the neutron detector one bin off, so the calculation-to-experiment ratios it printed were wrong with no warning. It now sums the partial tally over cells, scores the net current and reads bin j for upper edge j; the case had not been published.

defects.title: The reported highest piece was the noisiest, not the one the run tracked
defects.disposition: The report ranked pieces by raw flux, while the worker ranks them by flux less two standard errors, so a poorly resolved piece could be shown as the highest and judged against the limit. The report now uses the same ranking (leading_peak); the result stays on the unfavourable side and is no longer inconsistent with the run's own stopping rule.

defects.title: The aiming reason claimed a straight channel from the plasma to the magnets
defects.disposition: The aiming step also fires for a bent duct that neutrons cross without a collision, so "straight channel" in the reason, the tool description and the handbook was wrong. All three now describe a duct that neutrons cross without a collision.

defects.title: The job artifact scanner stopped counting at the cap, so growth was unmeasurable
defects.disposition: The scanner returned as soon as a total passed its limit, and the limits counted files already in the job's folders, so a large machine's transport run was refused for what earlier steps had left. The scanner now counts totals fully and the limits apply to growth from the start of the job.

defects.title: Large models' weight windows written into model.xml exceeded the 256 MiB file limit
defects.disposition: A machine 1.8 times the reference size has 475,695 voxels and 17 groups of window bounds; as text in the model file they passed the job runner's single-file limit and the run died with "File too large". The windows now go to an HDF5 file named by relative path, and results are unchanged for a given seed.

defects.title: faris doctor said transport and Core execution were not implemented
defects.disposition: The doctor note was left from before those commands existed and told users the tools could not run. It now names the commands that run tools and says the desktop app's Find tools searches environments as well as PATH.

defects.title: Aiming visibility runs left their statepoints in the run folder and tripped its 512 MB limit
defects.disposition: On the 2000 MW test model each aiming target's visibility run left about 90 MB (model, statepoint, summary), 406 MB for five targets, and the run step stopped with ArtifactLimit. Each run's bulky files are now removed once its tally is read, unless the runs are kept on purpose.

defects.title: Transport stop rule could accept a run while one heavy history dominated the sum
defects.disposition: On the 2000 MW test model the error on the coil mean fell to 5.5 % and then jumped to 28 % when one history landed; a run that reached 5 % just after such a jump would have been accepted with an unreliable error. The stop rule now also needs the variance of the variance of the batch values at or below 0.1. Open because a heavy history not yet sampled cannot be seen from batch values: closing it needs a history-level tail check (MCNP's slope of the largest scores) or a weight ceiling in the aimed windows. Cause found 2026-10-14 (seed 21, batch 73: 72 % of the batch in tf-coil-00 beside the port duct): the aiming patch let a particle headed at the duct skip the windows even inside a coil, so it scored its whole weight. The patch now skips windows only in void (integrations/openmc/patches/faris-openmc-0.15.3-aim.patch). Bent-duct model, three seeds against a stock run: summed coil flux z -1.14 (pooled), no bias seen. Large model, same seed: the batch is still heavy (18x the median instead of 38x; error 5.1 % to 17.9 %), so a second path remains. Second cause, traced on the large model (every track of batch 73 recorded): one source neutron gave 94 % of the batch's coil score. It struck the first wall 15 cm outside the port mouth, where the coarse windows are far too high, survived roulette 210 times heavier (0.30 to 62.7), and reached coils 00 and 17 split into 8,012 copies. Fix: design transport caps a roulette survivor at 5 times the weight it replaces (OPENMC_WW_ROULETTE_FACTOR, ROULETTE_FACTOR in integrations/openmc/design_transport.py; MCNP limits one split or roulette to 5). Large model, same seed, with the cap: heaviest batch 3.4 times the median (was 18 and 38), variance of the variance 0.027, mean error 4.3 % with no jump, summed coil flux 3.00e15 +/- 3.3 % against 3.20e15 +/- 10 % before (z -0.6). Bent duct with the cap, two seeds against the stock run: pooled z -1.45. Remaining, not this defect: the large model's peak piece needs more than the 1 h limit to reach 10 % (11.7 %), and the port mouth needs finer windows (NUC-079).

defects.title: Malformed Monte Carlo uncertainty bypassed the validation precision check
defects.disposition: A supplied NaN, infinity or negative Monte Carlo uncertainty was silently ignored by the compatibility precision check and could produce PASS. Supplied non-finite, negative and boolean uncertainties now produce INCONCLUSIVE with a reason and next step. The regression reproduced PASS for NaN, infinity and negative uncertainty before the fix; the validation suite passes after it.

defects.title: Release gate ignored the approved validation-access outcome
defects.disposition: The gate extracted VAL-023 from the approved release list but ignored its explicit access-outcome alternative, requiring Met even when the authorized outcome was recorded. The gate now checks the narrowly authorized, hash-pinned access evidence and accounts for its trace separately while retaining NOT_EVALUATED and not-validated matrix rows. Other requirements still require Met. The original checker rejected the controlled complete access fixture; the corrected checker accepts that condition without changing its No requirement status or physical validation state.

defects.title: Overlapping component replacements counted plant downtime more than once
defects.disposition: Maintenance summaries and duration sensitivities summed concurrent component outages, understating plant replacement availability without a warning. They now use the clipped union of replacement intervals. The controlled actual HistoryResult regression failed before the fix (21 s instead of 18 s downtime) and passed after it; availability changes from 79 to 82 percent over its 100 s horizon. Per-component event records and archived result files are unchanged.

defects.title: Cold ACTINV prepared-cache creation exceeds the external-job file limit
defects.disposition: Cold ACTINV preparation creates a 275493400-byte library.actp, larger than the ordinary 256 MiB file cap. ACTINV now has a separate checked prepared-cache root with a 320 MiB per-file, 1 GiB aggregate and 256-file cap; ordinary artifacts retain their original limits. Symlinks and special files are refused, cancellation remains bounded, and atomic cache publication is handled. The initial cold execution failed at the ordinary cap. A fresh empty-cache live ACTINV reproducibility regression now passes, creating the verified prepared library and spectrum cache; this establishes cold execution, not experimental activation validation.

defects.title: ACTINV jobs ignored documented cache-root overrides
defects.disposition: The restricted job environment omitted ACTINV_CACHE_DIR and platform cache roots, so an explicitly configured prepared cache was ignored. Both adapters now use one allowlist that preserves documented cache roots, checked data configuration and platform environment-name behavior without inheriting unrelated variables. The controlled old allowlist failed the regression; the corrected allowlist and warm-cache live adapter tests pass. Cold preparation is tracked separately as FARIS-014.

defects.title: Short target-error CAD runs bypassed the final lost-particle fraction guard
defects.disposition: An in-progress loss warmup also applied at finalization, so a target-error or budget stop before one million histories could be accepted above the one-in-a-million lost fraction. Finalization now checks the actual final fraction strictly above 1e-6 at any positive history count. The actual phase_run fixture with 1 lost neutron in 600000 histories failed before the fix and now reports lost_particles, target_reached false and geometry guidance.

defects.title: Lost-particle diagnostics described birth positions as escape locations
defects.disposition: OpenMC particle files record birth positions, but FARIS told users to inspect the model where particles were lost. The worker guidance, shared report and native view now label those coordinates as birth points and do not imply they identify the escape boundary. The old wording failed the controlled guidance regression; worker-assembly and CLI/native presentation tests now preserve that distinction.

defects.title: R3 aggregate dose errors discarded covariance between spatial and parent bins
defects.disposition: The historical reference producers combined marginal bin errors in quadrature after spatial and parent weighting, which is invalid for correlated scores. Prospective producers now aggregate within each completed batch before estimating the standard error. The fully correlated synthetic control gives standard error 5 instead of the former 2.915 quadrature. Historical central values and archived files remain unchanged; their uncertainty estimates require requalification. Unknown D1S/R2S covariance gives INCONCLUSIVE and no propagated ratio error. R2S photon error remains explicitly conditional on its generated activation source.

defects.title: Legacy R3 reference methods were described as selecting equivalent decay-emitter domains
defects.disposition: D1S MeshBornFilter follows each current particle birth, including secondary interaction sites, while the legacy R2S source activated only the response box. The old equivalence claim is retracted and those outputs are retained only as diagnostics. The prospective full-emission protocol removes the D1S birth filter and separately spans verified H5M geometry with the R2S activation mesh; the exporter refuses legacy or hidden birth-filter inputs. This corrects input qualification and interpretation, not physical dose validation: matched solver runs and source-resolution convergence remain pending under VAL-043.

defects.title: H5M material metadata lookup ignored direct material-group contents
defects.disposition: The H5M reader looked for physical volumes among a material group's children although MOAB stores them in the group's direct contents, so real torus volumes had no material tag. It now reads direct membership and excludes implicit complement groups. The reference builder also checks expected tags when matching CAD roles. The actual old-reader regression failed with a missing steel tag and the corrected reader passed; the exact-mesh retag control preserved all geometry datasets.

defects.title: Heating closure parser accepted an explicitly failed three-standard-error gate
defects.disposition: The native heating parser checked agreement between the closure flag and inequality but returned that agreement as success even when both indicated failure. It now requires the actual correlated closure inequality to pass and the recorded flag to be true. The controlled failed-closure worker fixture failed before the correction and passes after it by preserving INCONCLUSIVE rather than accepting the result.

defects.title: DAGMC conversion wrote faceting tolerance under an unread tag and root handle
defects.disposition: The converter emitted a bounding-box heuristic as FACETING_TOLERANCE instead of the declared mesher input. The first correction also attached the tag to null handle zero, so the selected DagMC reader still reported an invalid tiny value. The corrected copy now records sparse FACETING_TOL on the actual serialized geometry root set; the producer remains unchanged and all other dataset identities are checked. A live torus control reproduces the bad value before correction and prints exactly 0.05 afterwards, with the geometry-only stochastic-volume control completing. This records the requested tolerance, not a certified maximum deviation.

defects.title: Event-specific dose worker failed before neutron transport
defects.disposition: The normal request path used chain_coverage before assigning it. The same checked-request fixture fails on the original code with UnboundLocalError and reaches the mocked neutron stage after correction. Coverage is now computed before expensive transport from actual model roots and their reachable products; unavailable data remain NOT_EVALUATED. This fixes execution order, not dose validation.

defects.title: Heating batch storage grew with the number of batches
defects.disposition: The coupled-heating collector retained every per-voxel batch array, so large requested runs could exhaust the bounded worker memory. Fixed-size online moments now preserve mean, standard error and same-batch correlated closure residuals. A 20000-batch regression verifies fixed state shape and independent sequence controls verify its numerical moments; preflight bounds reject oversized meshes before volume sampling.

defects.title: Heating volume samples were not bound to the sampled H5M bytes
defects.disposition: A geometry change during the separate volume phase followed by restoration could pair volumes from one geometry with transport on another without an identity warning. Heating now takes a verified immutable snapshot for volume sampling and transport preparation, checks its bytes before and after use, and binds the volume receipt to READY preflight. A transient mutation/restoration fixture is refused.

defects.title: R3 R2S silently omitted neutron reactions on activated daughters
defects.disposition: R3 requested MicroXS for initial material nuclides only; missing daughter cross sections were silently treated as zero even over the one-FPY irradiation. The runner now derives reachable nuclides and required channels, refuses incomplete coverage before transport, requests the full required set, and records actual MicroXS membership. Export independently checks the bound data and membership. An in-band legacy record without that evidence is refused. Current installed inputs remain NOT_EVALUATED with 2168 missing nuclides and 12 missing indexed MT groups; historical results are diagnostic and require requalification.

defects.title: Convex-face bound used a length tolerance on an area-valued cross product
defects.disposition: The planar fast path could classify points far outside a very short polygon edge as inside, understating the whole-triangle deviation. Signed half-plane distances and convexity checks are now normalized by edge length, with separate outward kernel and arithmetic allowances. The short-edge outside-point and shallow-concavity regressions pass; unsupported trims still fall back to bounded subdivision.

defects.title: Restarted study transport read batch counters before restart restoration
defects.disposition: Reading current_batch immediately after openmc_init returned zero for a restarted pass, so the new loss-accounting receipt did not match the actual restart. The selected executable-linked C API now initializes the simulation, captures restored counters, advances batches explicitly, and records per-pass loss deltas before finalization. A live control verifies clean zero-loss passes and intentional all-loss passes of 1000 and 2000 histories across the restart using the selected library, not the different Python-packaged library.

defects.title: Solver capture receipts retained private byte buffers and could not serialize
defects.disposition: Completed solver captures exposed an internal pending bytes buffer in the JSON receipt, causing final run-record serialization to fail after transport. The buffer is removed after final stream flushing; bounded logs, warning counts and hashes remain. A real subprocess regression checks trailing fragments and JSON serialization, and the selected-library restart/loss control now writes its complete report successfully.

defects.title: Transport enclosing sphere clipped mixed-sign model extents
defects.disposition: The generic model builder sized its bounding sphere from only the lower and upper diagonal corners. With mixed-sign extents another corner can be farther from the origin, leaving part of the requested geometry outside the vacuum boundary. The sphere now uses every coordinate extremum. The mixed-sign regression checks that all eight corners remain inside. This corrects the geometry domain for flux, heating and dose preparation; affected physical results require fresh qualification.

defects.title: Thin material photon-source regions hit the default OpenMC rejection cutoff
defects.disposition: Exact material-constrained box resampling can occupy less than the OpenMC default accepted-to-rejected proposal threshold. A live one-percent-cell control aborts with the default and samples all 1000 sites inside the same cell with the configured 1e-6 threshold. The photon worker records that execution setting and retains the exact conditional distribution and absolute ACTINV source strengths. Very thin regions can still sample slowly or fail closed; this is execution evidence, not physical dose validation.

defects.title: FNS decay-heat provenance recorded the wrong source PDF hash
defects.disposition: The FARIS manifest and builder copied an incorrect original PDF hash even though the pinned upstream processing note contained the correct value. The earlier preflight checked the note identity without checking its member table and accepted that mismatch. The corrected preflight derives all four member identities from the verified upstream note and refuses inconsistent metadata. A retained old-manifest control is refused and the corrected pinned-source plan passes; measured values, spectrum and scoring criteria are unchanged. No solver run used the incorrect provenance.

defects.title: ITER reference intake accepted changed benchmark inputs without checking registered identities
defects.disposition: The reference runner accepted files by name and recorded their observed hashes without requiring the registered upstream identities. Changed same-shaped source or geometry files could therefore be run under the ITER_1D reference label. Intake now checks all four translated files and benchmark metadata against the reference registration and case manifest, then rechecks the staged copies before transport. Same-size input and copied-file mutations are refused. Both 97-cell flux and absorption responses are required; no reference values or scientific results were added.

defects.title: Bounded activation cleanup discarded material identities before writing receipts
defects.disposition: The new bounded R3 activation stage deleted its material list before recording activation material IDs and tried to delete an undefined local. Its first chunk would fail before a usable activation record was written. Cleanup now follows receipt construction and preserves all material IDs. An end-to-end mocked execution runs two chunks through receipt writing and checks final-step and source-state behavior. No physical campaign consumed the broken path.

defects.title: Rank-deficient heating covariance was refused after floating-point cancellation
defects.disposition: The whole-model partition closure subtracted large correlated covariance terms and compared their near-zero contrast without a roundoff bound. Valid rank-deficient responses could fail closed. Compensated contraction now retains the absolute term sum and applies a floating-point error bound while rejecting material covariance inconsistencies. The native regression passes after its authored means and sampling errors were made internally consistent; this does not qualify transport physics.

defects.title: Combined history energy trusted edited heating-report numbers without rechecking raw worker evidence
defects.disposition: The new heat-to-history combination could consume edited report response numbers without comparing them to the retained worker result and request. Combination now rehashes retained request/result files, validates their source and sampling context, compares the exact response, and carries supplemental heating provenance into history results. The native mutation regression passes. No qualified physical result was produced through the broken path.

defects.title: FNS finite-detector flux omitted the spherical-volume normalization
defects.disposition: OpenMC cell-filter flux is tracklength integrated over the detector volume. The adapter applied the source FM and lethargy width without dividing the mean and standard deviation by that volume, giving the wrong response units and radius dependence. Both now use the exact analytic sphere volume; raw scores, units, radius and volume remain in receipts. Analytic and radius-invariance regressions pass. The first live pilot remains unsealed and unqualified due to sparse tallies; F5 point-estimator equivalence and the unchanged convergence criteria remain separate requirements.

defects.title: AIM vacuum control and production preflight disagreed with the documented CLI and runtime identity
defects.disposition: The new optional control referenced a case argument absent from its real parser, and its runtime identity contained Python fields missing from production preflight. The documented command failed before transport, while production would refuse a valid control on the same runtime. Scope now comes from the verified manifest and both paths share the complete runtime preflight. Parser-backed and identity regressions pass; the actual twelve-response vacuum control and its raw-statepoint consumer revalidation pass. The material benchmark remains unqualified.
